title: North Dakota AI Laws

reading.body:
North Dakota's only AI law is narrow: it requires a disclaimer on political ads that use AI to impersonate a human, and it exempts ordinary text and editing tools.

The pattern is disclosure, not restriction. HB1167, passed 2025-04-11, does not regulate how AI systems are built or run. It targets one output, a political communication containing digital content that visually or audibly impersonates a human, and requires a prominent disclaimer on it. The exemptions matter as much as the requirement: text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, and enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation are carved out. That is a deliberate line between synthetic media that fabricates a person and software that edits words.

For AI specifically, this is a content-integrity rule, not a compute rule. Nothing in the enrolled text touches data centers, electricity, model training, or the physical infrastructure that constrains AI scaling. A state can pass this kind of law without engaging the grid question at all, and North Dakota has.

What the data does not cover: one law is a thin basis for characterizing a state's posture. It says nothing about pending bills, agency rules, or federal preemption, and the count reflects only what this site judged relevant to AI. Read it as a single enacted disclosure requirement, not as a regulatory regime.

North Dakota has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in North Dakota

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB1167: Artificial intelligence disclosure statements. passed 2025-04-11

    This North Dakota law requires a prominent disclaimer on political communications and advertising that contain digital content created in whole or in part with artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human. It exempts certain uses of artificial intelligence for text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation. It defines artificial intelligence for this purpose.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for North Dakota. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
